chapter: Road bands: Hucklebuck Williams and Tiny Bradshaw
title: Bradshaw's "three sons" and lending his Lincoln
summary: The three young clean-living players are treated as sons, drive Bradshaw's Lincoln between gigs, and learn how to carry themselves.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: We travelled man, we travelled. And we travelled clean and uh, cause if we wasn't working we'd be in the streets. We'd be clean and he liked that.
You see. And the--and he, and he called us our--say those are my three sons there, you know.
And uh, and we would wear suits and stuff, man so he'd--wow--that'd knock him out, you know.

And uh, and then he began to say take my car to the next gig. And give us some money. And this is something, man, he--out of twenty something years, he had a piano player playing with him--played with him for twenty-two years, man. Beewee Robinson. [Jimmy Robinson]
He say "man, this is something Bradshaw ain't never did--let nobody drive his automobile nowhere," you know.
And he would give us his car cause he wants to hang out with a lady or something, you know.
And he'd be there the next day on the plane.
Take my car to the next gig. So we would take the car, you know ... We'd drive in town, man, with this big Lincoln. He had a Lincoln, man, you know the Continental kit and stuff.

And stuff. And me, Bill Hardman and Paul, man, cat on in town, man. And he taught--he taught--he taught me a lot, man, about this business and uh, and how to be a musician. How to really carry myself to, you know, to, to, to, really make a living out here and, you know.
